constraints.note: Brief applied as hard limits: 5 topics, 7 clips (5 full + 2 impact, cap was 8), every clip UNDER 70 s. The longest RAW cut is 64.82 s (clip 5) and the tighten pass only removes time, so no clip can finish at 70 s or over. Selection leans on coin hype and conviction, per the doctrine: this was a 63-minute dump-day stream and most of it is ordinary market talk (midterms vs IPO, weekly close, where the bottom is), which is all in dropped[]. Ranks 1-3 are the real picks; ranks 4-5 are thinner and fine to kill. Political and personal tangents, the membership pitch and the creator call-out are out; there was no ElizaOS talk in this stream.

topics.hook_summary: I've been saying it, I'll just keep saying it: Pengu is gonna flip Pepe. From a 300 million market cap it could be like a 100x, it could get to 30 billion, and I'm really serious. I bought more.

I never imagined some of these things would be so low right now, but OREO is still up from my call, and Pieverse is almost unaffected by the dump: if you were in my group, you'd be up 10x on this right now.

A big wallet has started to receive Kaspa deposits again. They're getting ready for something. Smart money keeps building and things are gonna pop. There's a bright future for Kaspa, just a lot of pain right now.
JCT was like a 6x overnight last week and it returned to its low. Good time for you guys to get in. It's a freebie; my community members, we got the 6x.
We've been dumping and I've been buying a whole bunch of plays at really low prices. Litecoin at $45 is insanely low, and Arbitrum from 900 million to 10 billion is a 10x, relatively safe.

clips.title: Pengu Is Gonna Flip Pepe. I Bought More at 300 Million

segments.why: Cold-open hook, lifted from later in the run: 'I've been saying it, man. I'll just keep saying it. Pengu is gonna flip Pepe. It's gonna be one of the biggest meme coins.'
The action behind the claim: 'I put in Pengu. I bought a little bit more Pengu.'

The reasoning and the number: 'I think this is going to be like a powerhouse... in the next run-up, 300 million market cap... it could be like a 100x, it could get to 30 billion. I'm really serious with Pengu.' Skips the slow 'very insider intense VC backed' aside at 1956.5-1961.8.

Humor button right after the 100x claim: 'Never financial advice. Holy crap. Guys, remember, you gotta remind me to punch in the goddamn balls. Never financial advice around here.' Out-point sits in a 100 ms gap before he repeats 'never never ever financial'.
Closer: 'I got me some more Pengu. I think Pengu at 300 million's a steal.'

peak_beats.note: Pengu is gonna flip Pepe. It's gonna be one of the biggest meme coins.
It could be like a 100x, it could get to 30 billion. I'm really serious with Pengu.

clips.notes: Emotional core = segment 0 (the doubling 'I've been saying it, I've been saying it, I'll just keep saying it' reads as peak conviction) plus the 100x / 30 billion line inside segment 2. Assembly is non-chronological on purpose: the flip-Pepe claim opens cold, then the buy, the reasoning, the disclaimer gag, and it ends on 'a steal'. The 'But we shall see' hedge at 1998.5-1999.9 is cut. If the punch-in-the-balls gag feels like an inside joke for a cold viewer, drop segment 3 (clip becomes 39.26 s).

clips.title: Everything Is Low Right Now. These Calls Are Still Up

segments.why: Setup and first receipt: 'I never imagined that some of these things would be so low right now. OREO... one of my excellent plays. Still up from my call. Look at that. Holy crap. Still up from my call. OREO. Unbelievable.'

Escalation: 'I did my Pieverse video. Pieverse doing pretty good right now, $1.91... Look at this weekly. It's almost unaffected from the dumps... when you see a coin like this, man, that's awesome. This is one of my plays. If you were in my group, you'd be up 10x on this right now.' Ends on the 10x line; the membership pitch that follows (1911.8-1941.3) is excluded.

peak_beats.note: When you see a coin like this, man, that's awesome. This is one of my plays. If you were in my group, you'd be up 10x on this right now.
Still up from my call. Look at that. Holy crap. OREO. Unbelievable.

clips.notes: Scatter-gather across 10 minutes: two separate moments where he checks one of his own calls in the middle of the dump and it is still up. Emotional core = the Pieverse 10x line (end of segment 1), with the OREO 'Holy crap... unbelievable' disbelief as the second beat. Segment 1 has around 12 s of chart-loading dead air (1856.9-1857.9, 1859.7-1862.2, 1865.6-1867.5, 1875.2-1880.0, 1884.3-1887.7) for the tighten pass; expect around 45 s final. Left out on purpose: the unnamed 'two other coins up a few hundred percent' (1892.6-1910.3, 634-659), which gives a cold viewer nothing to look up.

clips.title: They Are Getting Ready for Something on Kaspa

segments.why: News hook, read off a tweet on screen: 'In a strange turn of events, the [MARA?] wallet has started to receive Kaspa deposits. This could indicate them turning mining machines on again, or simply receiving a final payout from the pool.' Wallet name needs confirmation from Mike (see review_callouts).
His read on it: 'They're getting ready for something, right? They're ready for something, but...' (the trailing 'but' runs into 'there's a lot, you know' at the top of the next segment).

Conviction: 'There's a lot... you know, smart money keeps building. They keep doing this thing, they keep investing, and I think things are just gonna pop, man. Things are gonna pop. And it's like 2027 is gonna be awesome.'
The pain, from 42 minutes later: 'We've been like this for too long. We never got a break. Keep getting beaten over the head, as I keep saying.'

Resolve: 'There's a bright future for Kaspa. Just a lot of pain right now.' In-point is after his 1.7 s pause, so the viewer comment he was reading ('Kaspa come to a tier 1 exchange, mark my words') stays out.
Button: 'Yeah, it's always good to buy more Kaspa.'

peak_beats.note: I think things are just gonna pop, man. Things are gonna pop. And it's like 2027 is gonna be awesome.
We've been like this for too long. We never got a break. Keep getting beaten over the head.

clips.notes: The only Kaspa material in this stream with conviction in it, gathered from four points (13:41, 44:41, 55:36, 56:10). Emotional core = segment 2 (the doubled 'things are gonna pop') and segment 3 (the pain line). Segment 0 is a flat tweet read and he hedges it himself ('I don't know, man', cut at 837.2-843.5), so it is there as the news hook, not for energy. If the tweet fails the check, kill this clip and keep clip 7, which is the same arc without the tweet.

clips.title: JCT Did a 6x Overnight. Now It's Back at Its Low

segments.why: Hook: 'JCT, how's JCT doing? We had a huge pump on this. It was like a 6x overnight last week. How is it right now?' In-point sits in a 100 ms dip between 'yeah' and 'JCT' in running speech; tighten pass to verify the first syllable.

Payoff after the chart loads: 'It returned to its low. Look at that. So, good time for you guys to get in, right? It's a freebie, if you're not in my community. My community members, we got the 6x. This is in the compute narrative.'

peak_beats.note: Good time for you guys to get in. It's a freebie, right? If you're not in my community. My community members, we got the 6x.

clips.notes: A punch, not a build: question, reveal, call. Emotional core = the 'It's a freebie' beat in segment 1. The cut between the segments removes 5.2 s of silence while the chart loads. Ends on 'the compute narrative' so the viewer gets one reason beyond price; a harder out is 3087.85 ('we got the 6x'). The half-finished 'everything has their own little narrative and the compute narrative...' after it is left out.

clips.title: We've Been Dumping and I've Been Buying

segments.why: Cold-open hook from minute 2: 'We've been dumping. We have been dumping. And I've been buying a whole bunch of plays at really low prices. Really, really low prices.' Picture checked: BTC chart with the red candles plus face cam, not the countdown card.
Thesis and first name: 'They all got their little things. Like, Litecoin right now is an optional privacy coin, which is great.'
Personal story: 'I think Litecoin is a good play. I got into this again. After all these years, I was shocked that I did it. But I think it's pretty good, especially with that news.'
The number: 'To get Litecoin at $45 right now, that's insanely low. That is like so low.'
Second name: 'Another one that I got into recently, Arbitrum. This is the tokenized assets narrative. Robinhood is using the Arbitrum tech.'
Payoff: 'If you get in now, you get in kind of low, and they're good for some good pumps, right? It was 900 million at Arbitrum. What if it goes to 10 billion, you got a 10x? Relatively safe.'

peak_beats.note: It was 900 million at Arbitrum. What if it goes to 10 billion, you got a 10x? Relatively safe.
Litecoin at $45 right now, that's insanely low. That is like so low.

clips.notes: Weakest of the five and the first one to kill if the delivery is flat: it is closer to 'what I bought this week' than to hyping one coin. It earns the slot on the opener (segment 0, buying while everyone dumps), the Litecoin story (a Kaspa guy back in Litecoin 'after all these years') and the Arbitrum 10x line. Emotional core = segment 0 and segment 3. Longest clip in the plan at 64.82 s raw; the tighten pass only shortens it. To stay under 70 s, 'they all have their little narratives, a lot of them are really bullish' (2794.5-2799.0) and 'a lot of things are at a discount' (2707.4-2712.0) were left out; either can replace segment 0 if Mike wants the clip to stay inside one stretch of the stream.

clips.title: There's a Bright Future for Kaspa. Just a Lot of Pain Right Now

segments.why: opens on the pain: 'We've been like this for too long. We never got a break. Keep getting beaten over the head, as I keep saying.'
the turn: 'Smart money keeps building. They keep investing, and I think things are just gonna pop, man. Things are gonna pop. 2027 is gonna be awesome.'

button: 'It's always good to buy more Kaspa.'

clips.notes: The stick-through-the-pain cut: clip 3 without the tweet, re-ordered to open on the pain line. It exists so there is a Kaspa short that does not depend on the wallet claim. Emotional core = segment 0 into the doubled 'things are gonna pop' in segment 1. Kaspa is first named in segment 2, so the title and caption carry the name up front.

review_callouts: ENERGY IS UNVERIFIED on all 7 clips (text-first pass; three stills were pulled only to check the picture, no audio was listened to). Cores to confirm: clip 1 seg 0, clip 2 end of seg 1, clip 3 seg 2 and seg 3, clip 4 'It's a freebie', clip 5 seg 0 and seg 3.

CLIP 3, confirm before anything else: Whisper heard 'the malware wallet has started to receive Kaspa deposits'. From context (mining machines, pool payout) it is probably 'the MARA wallet' (Marathon), but that is a guess. Mike must confirm the name, and that he is fine leading a short on a third-party tweet he hedged on stream. If not: delete clip 3, keep clip 7.
CLIP 4 is time-sensitive: 'it returned to its low, good time to get in' is only true while JCT is still near that low. Check the price before it queues, or post it first.

CLIP 5: at 46:53 Whisper has him saying Arbitrum goes 'to like 10 million' for a 10x from 900 million. He means 10 billion; listen to what is actually audible and caption accordingly. His own words 'relatively safe' close the clip, which is a call for Mike.

CLIP 2: the on-screen chat bubble around 21:10 reads 'I still have my Cooper lol' (a viewer comment, visible in the still at 21:10). He also says 'the dumps yesterday' at 31:13; the day-relative word is in the audio only and is kept out of the title.
CLIP 2 and CLIP 4: 'if you were in my group you'd be up 10x' and 'my community members, we got the 6x' are community-win lines, kept on purpose; the actual membership pitch (31:52-32:21) is excluded.

Background music is on under parts of the stream (audible bed around 21:00, 51:00 and 55:36; silent at 13:41, 33:00, 44:41, 45:25). Clips 2, 3, 4 and 7 join bed and no-bed segments; listen for the bed popping in and out at the joins.

Cut points were snapped to measured silences in the master audio (the mic is gated), not to raw Whisper word times. Two in/out points sit in gaps of only around 100 ms inside running speech and need the tighten pass to confirm no clipped syllable: clip 4 in-point (3054.56) and clip 1 seg 3 out-point (2009.86).
Thin stream: around 50 of the 63 minutes is market narration or chat. If Mike wants fewer, the kill order is clip 5, clip 4, then one of each full/impact pair (6 or 1, 7 or 3).
